brief: My balcony is full sun with low moisture, and one cat lives in the household. A south-facing balcony in summer gets brutal sun all day and the wind dries the soil quickly. One elderly cat, indoor, but I also worry about a stray.

design.site_summary: A sunny, low-moisture urban balcony designed to be completely safe for curious household pets.
design.layout_strategy: The scheme stacks a mid-level wall arrangement of upright shrubs and herbs at waist height, a structural floor-level accent of succulents and grasses, and a grazing zone placed directly on the floor for easy pet access.
design.combination_logic: The design contrasts the fine, silvery spikes of grass and fragrant needle foliage of rosemary with the fleshy, architectural rosettes of succulents and soft herbs, creating a dynamic interplay of textures and aromatic scents that provide year-round visual interest.

zones.placement: Against the back wall, facing full sun with 6 hours of direct afternoon light.

plants.why: Thrives in full sun and low moisture while offering wonderful fragrance.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides vertical height, woody structure, and a strong evergreen aromatic presence against the wall.

plants.why: Loves partial shade to full sun and matches the low-water requirement of the zone.
plants.role_in_combination: Introduces soft grey-green textural contrast and velvety leaves that soften the woody stems of the rosemary.

maintenance: Water thoroughly only when the top two inches of soil are dry.
Prune back woody stems lightly after flowering to maintain shape.
Feed with a balanced low-nitrogen organic fertilizer once in spring.

zones.placement: In the western corner of the balcony floor, receiving bright indirect light and partial sun.

plants.why: Forms tight, low-growing rosettes that tolerate dry conditions exceptionally well.
plants.role_in_combination: Creates a sculptural ground-level carpet of pale blue-green rosettes that contrast with upright grasses.

plants.why: Adds dramatic height and architectural presence at floor level.
plants.role_in_combination: Brings feathery plumes and tall, arching linear foliage that breaks up the low horizontal lines of the succulents.

maintenance: Water sparingly, allowing soil to dry out completely between waterings.
Remove dead lower leaves from succulents as needed.
Cut back the pampas grass foliage in late winter before new growth starts.

zones.placement: On the open balcony floor within easy reach of the pet, set in partial shade.

plants.why: Provides a low, sweet-scented herb layer that is entirely safe and engaging for pets to nibble.
plants.role_in_combination: Offers a delicate carpet of tiny flowers and soft foliage that carpets the base of the pet tray.

plants.why: Provides an intriguing trunk shape and cascading leaves that pets can safely interact with.
plants.role_in_combination: Acts as a central anchor in the grazing tray with fun, ribbon-like foliage.

maintenance: Water lightly twice a week during warm summer months and weekly in spring.
Trim spent flower heads on the alyssum to encourage continuous blooming.
Repot the ponytail palm every two to three years into slightly larger containers.

care_instructions.task: Check soil moisture across all containers to prevent drought stress or waterlogging.
care_instructions.frequency: Twice a week in summer, weekly in spring and autumn.

care_instructions.task: Apply an organic, slow-release fertilizer to support vigorous foliage and root growth.
care_instructions.frequency: Monthly during the active growing phase.

care_instructions.task: Inspect plants for any signs of dust or debris on leaves and wipe gently.

care_cautions: Overwatering the Echeveria elegans and Haworthia species in the ground-level containers can quickly lead to root rot.
The Rosmarinus officinalis and Salvia officinalis on the hot wall may suffer from extreme scorch if underwatered during peak summer heatwaves.
design.pet_safety_note: Every plant included in this scheme is rigorously verified as 100 percent non-toxic to cats and dogs, ensuring a completely safe environment even if your pet decides to graze.
